summary: The serving path itself is the right shape: DIRECT opens the sink, writes nothing, completes, and buys no object-store request (presign is deliberately uncounted by CountingBinStore and ADR-0041 says signing issues no request, so the zero is honest rather than an artefact of the meter). The routing line is safe for every production configuration: DefaultIngest builds its policy from FetchPolicyConfig.defaultsFor, whose inline cap is 256 KiB and whose cross-AZ crossover is derived, so Long.MAX_VALUE > min(cap, crossover) and a cold segment still answers PROXY exactly as `heldBytes == null ? PROXY` did, with directEnabled false making wantsDirect return before the fan-out arm is read. Three things do not hold. (1) The coalescing claim is measured against a Subscriber shape no caller in the tree has: grouping is by Subscriber IDENTITY, and every transport in the tree registers a fresh `assembling` subscriber per RunKey, so a node with K shards is K targets and gets K grants -- the shards-per-node number M5.39 handed here, not the per-node one the cell claims falls out by construction. (2) The new Push invariant breaks SubscriptionHub.assembling, which rebuilds a Push with the six-argument form and no grant, so the first DIRECT delivery to the tree's own consumer adapter throws inside complete() and is swallowed as a slow subscriber. (3) The Long.MAX_VALUE sentinel is a `<=` away from meaning its opposite: six in-tree fixtures configure both caps at Long.MAX_VALUE, and on those a cold segment now answers INLINE, calls writeHeldBytes(null, ...), swallows the NPE per sink and completes every subscriber with zero bytes -- the exact empty-push failure the cell says Long.MAX_VALUE fixed, moved from every config to one.

findings.title: one grant per Subscriber is not one grant per node, because every transport in the tree subscribes one Subscriber per RunKey
findings.failure_scenario: publishSegment groups by ByIdentity(subscriber) (SubscriptionHub.java:380-410), and every SubscriptionTransport in the tree builds a NEW subscriber per key: `HUB.subscribe(key, SubscriptionHub.assembling(...))` in ShardFanOutIT:75, SearchableIT, RestartResumeIT, OffsetMonotonicityIT, and the same shape behind NodeSubscriptions.clientFor, which makes one ConsumerClient per RunKey. So an OpenSearch node holding 20 (or 64, or ~400) runs of one segment is 20 distinct Subscriber instances, hence 20 Targets, hence 20 iterations of this loop and 20 mintGrant calls for ONE segment -- a grant count in shards-per-node, which is precisely the rate M5.39 handed to this row and which non-negotiable 6 forbids by name. The new test cannot see it: KRunsOnONEConsumerCostONEGrantNotK (DirectServingTest.java:52) passes ONE shared `oneNode` lambda to 64 subscribe() calls, a shape no caller in the tree uses, and M5.40a's own cell already records the measurement -- 'every caller in the tree subscribes one RunKey per Subscriber, so K is always 1'. The comment at 563-572 ('minting once per iteration is once per consumer') and the backlog cell ('THE COALESCING RULE FALLS OUT BY CONSTRUCTION ... once per (consumer, segment)') therefore assert a per-(node, segment) property the code does not have. The grant is a pure function of (segmentKey, ceiling) and is identical for every target, so hoisting the mint above the `for (Target t : targets)` loop makes one signature per segment -- flat by construction for ANY subscriber granularity, and still one grant per consumer -- or the cell must say plainly that node-level coalescing is NOT achieved here and name the row that owns it.

findings.title: the `direct`-push-without-a-grant refusal is reachable from SubscriptionHub.assembling, and the throw is swallowed
findings.failure_scenario: SubscriptionHub.assembling rebuilds each Push in complete() with the six-argument constructor -- `new Push(push.key(), push.segmentKey(), push.recordCount(), push.firstOffset(), push.via(), whole)` -- which delegates with grant = null while carrying via = DIRECT. The new compact-constructor guard at SubscriptionHub.java:103 then throws IllegalArgumentException('a `direct` push without a grant tells a consumer to fetch and not how') from inside complete(), and deliver's completion loop catches IOException | RuntimeException and continues. Concretely: a deployment with directEnabled = true on a presigning backend publishes a cold segment at fanOut 1; the hub elects DIRECT, opens the assembling sink, writes nothing, and then drops the consumer's callback entirely -- no onSegment, no log line, no undeliverablePushes increment (that counter only sees throws that escape publish). The consumer silently loses the whole window, which is the same silent-window failure M5.47's cell records for the removed one-argument publish. It is the adapter every IT bridge and M5.45e will drive all three modes through, so it fails the moment `direct` is switched on. One-line fix: pass push.grant() through, which is also the value the grant has to reach a consumer by.

findings.title: Long.MAX_VALUE still answers INLINE at the boundary, and the cold INLINE arm dereferences null bytes
findings.failure_scenario: FetchPolicy.modeFor takes `delivery.batchBytes() <= inlineBound`, with inlineBound = min(inlineCapBytes, crossAzCrossoverBytes) when bytesInServingAz is false. Long.MAX_VALUE <= Long.MAX_VALUE is TRUE, so a config whose two caps are both Long.MAX_VALUE now answers INLINE for a cold segment. Six fixtures in the tree are exactly that config -- SubscriptionHubTest.java:63, AssembledServingPathTest.java:177, OneStreamPerConsumerTest.java:335, EndToEndTest.java:231, ShardFanOutIT.java:178, SearchableIT.java:211 -- and none of them happens to publish a cold segment today, which is the only reason the suite is green. The next one that does (a batched delta whose heldSegmentKey is not the segment under test, or publish(delta, null, null, inlineForever)) takes `case INLINE -> writeHeldBytes(heldBytes, sinks)` with heldBytes == null; writeHeldBytes evaluates heldBytes.length inside its own try and swallows the NPE per sink, so every sink is completed having received ZERO bytes and the subscriber is handed an empty window with no error anywhere -- the identical failure the backlog cell attributes to the batchBytes = 0 attempt, narrowed from every config to this one and silent instead of loud. The comment's claim 'bytes this pod does not hold cannot be inlined AT ANY SIZE' is a statement about the caller, not about the policy, so it should be enforced at the caller: refuse INLINE structurally on the cold path (map it to PROXY, or give SegmentDelivery a bytes-in-hand component the policy reads) rather than relying on a sentinel that is one comparison away from meaning its opposite.

findings.title: a mint failure for one consumer denies the segment for all of them, and the null-issuer path still denies the rest of the delta
findings.failure_scenario: The mint sits ABOVE the try that exists to isolate exactly this class of per-consumer failure. If the backend's presign fails transiently while serving consumer i of n (an Azure user-delegation key fetch, say), mintGrant throws UncheckedIOException: consumers 1..i-1 already had open() called and are never completed and never told, consumers i..n are never opened at all, and publish records it as a per-segment failure. Moving the mint inside the existing try would make the blast radius one consumer, which is what the loop below it already does for a subscriber that throws on open. Separately, mintGrant's null-issuer branch throws IllegalStateException, which publish does NOT catch (it catches UncheckedIOException only), so that path denies every LATER segment of a batched delta -- and the comment at SubscriptionHub.java:322-325 still tells the reader 'The `DIRECT` arm below throws IllegalStateException and DOES still deny every later segment. M5.45d owns deciding what that arm becomes once it is live.' This row is M5.45d; the arm is live and the decision is not recorded anywhere.

findings.title: a directEnabled policy with a presigning backend and a null issuer is representable
findings.failure_scenario: The three-argument constructor pairs any policy with a null issuer. Build `new SegmentServing(new FetchPolicy(new FetchPolicyConfig(1, 1, 1, true)), presigningStore.capabilities(), proxy)` -- the shape DirectServingTest's own helper builds minus the issuer -- and the first cold publish elects DIRECT, hits mintGrant's null check and throws IllegalStateException at PUBLISH time, denying the rest of the delta, for a condition knowable at construction. DefaultIngest.java:247 keeps the two flags in step, but nothing else does, and non-negotiable 9 rung 1 asks for the bad state to be unrepresentable: the compact constructor can refuse issuer == null when policy.config().directEnabled() && capabilities.presignedUrls(), which is the same startup refusal GrantIssuer's own constructor performs one level down.

findings.title: criterion 1b is carried by a tautology and by a claim that is not true as stated
findings.failure_scenario: assertThat(pod.serving().issuer()).isSameAs(pod.serving().issuer()) compares two reads of the same final field and cannot fail under any mutation -- including one that built a fresh GrantIssuer per publish, since that would be inside publishSegment and invisible to this getter. What the case does constrain is presence/absence, which the two isNotNull/isNull assertions already carry. The accompanying claim, in the javadoc and repeated in the backlog cell, that 'per-publish construction is not representable', is false: publish takes SegmentServing as a PARAMETER, so any caller can construct one (and a GrantIssuer with it) per publish; what is true is the narrower and checkable statement that DefaultIngest has exactly one construction site. Also worth recording rather than fixing: both arms of the routing still pass servingPodUnderPressure = false, so FetchPolicy's load-shedding arm remains without a production caller and only the cold arm of `direct` is actually assembled.
